subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Notch Filters: Removing One Frequency
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Notch Filters: Removing One Frequency.

hook.text: A notch filter blocks just one frequency and passes everything else. A surgical cut.

buildup.text: The twin-T circuit creates a deep null at its design frequency. Rejection can exceed 40 dB.

discovery.text: The most common use: removing 50 or 60 Hz hum from power lines in audio recordings.

twist.text: Adaptive notch filters track a shifting interference frequency and cancel it in real time.

climax.text: ECG monitors, guitar effects, and lab instruments all use notch filters for clean signals.

punchline.text: Kill one frequency, save the rest — the notch filter is a precision scalpel.

quiz.question: What is the most common use of a 60 Hz notch filter?
options: Boosting bass frequencies in audio systems
Removing power-line hum from sensitive measurements
Tuning radio receivers to AM stations
